sources.title: The Farther Reaches of Human Nature
sources.author_or_publisher: Abraham H. Maslow / Human Potential Center
sources.supports: Search-indexed text of Maslow's essays, terminology, claims, examples, and late research programme.
sources.limitations: The host timed out during direct retrieval in this review, so important claims were triangulated with chapter records and later scholarship.

sources.title: The Farther Reaches of Human Nature
sources.supports: Contemporary description of the posthumous collection, recurring self-actualisation theme, normative proposals, method dispute, tone, and likely reception across psychological camps.
sources.limitations: Short contemporary review rather than a modern evidence audit.

sources.title: Maslow on Human Possibility
sources.supports: Contemporary reception, Maslow's role in selecting late papers, philosophical direction, freshness, and emphasis on higher human possibilities.
sources.limitations: Sympathetic humanist review with little adversarial empirical analysis.

sources.title: Maslow reconsidered: A review of research on the need hierarchy theory
sources.author_or_publisher: Mahmoud A. Wahba and Lawrence G. Bridwell; Organizational Behavior and Human Performance
sources.supports: Systematic early review finding partial support for a hierarchy and no longitudinal support for the gratification-activation proposition.
sources.limitations: Evaluates the need hierarchy, not every late claim about creativity, values, cognition, or transcendence.

sources.title: Critique of Self-Actualization Theory
sources.author_or_publisher: Abraham H. Maslow; Journal of Humanistic Education and Development
sources.supports: Maslow's own late concern that unproved axioms were being accepted as gospel and his invitation to empirical challenge.
sources.limitations: Unpublished 1966 paper released posthumously; abstract access only.

sources.title: The exemplar methodology: An approach to studying the leading edge of development
sources.author_or_publisher: L. T. Bronk; Psychology of Well-Being
sources.supports: Balanced methodological analysis of Maslow's twenty-one exemplars, including the value of studying exceptional development and the risks of subjective selection, missing comparison, and tautology.
sources.limitations: Methodological review rather than a replication of Maslow's complete account.

sources.title: Maslow and the Good Person
sources.author_or_publisher: William C. Compton; Journal of Humanistic Psychology
sources.supports: Modern review finding support for several traits associated with optimal development while identifying substantial cultural dependence and later work on transcendence.
sources.limitations: Published in a journal sympathetic to humanistic psychology and distinguishes trait support from validation of self-actualisation as one construct.

sources.title: Rediscovering the Later Version of Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs
sources.author_or_publisher: Mark E. Koltko-Rivera; Review of General Psychology
sources.supports: Historical evidence that late Maslow placed self-transcendence beyond self-actualisation and discussion of its possible value for motivation, altruism, wisdom, religion, and culture.
sources.limitations: Theoretical and historical recovery, not direct causal validation of the higher stage.

sources.title: Needs and Subjective Well-Being Around the World
sources.author_or_publisher: Louis Tay and Ed Diener; Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
sources.supports: Data from 123 countries associating fulfilment of multiple needs with well-being while finding largely independent contributions rather than a strict prerequisite order.
sources.limitations: Cross-sectional self-report associations do not establish innate needs, causal sequence, or Maslow's complete growth theory.

sources.title: Self-determination theory and the facilitation of intrinsic motivation, social development, and well-being
sources.author_or_publisher: Richard M. Ryan and Edward L. Deci; American Psychologist
sources.supports: A later, more operational research programme on autonomy, competence, relatedness, intrinsic motivation, social context, and psychological growth.
sources.limitations: Alternative framework rather than a direct test of Maslow's B-values and transcendence.

sources.title: Who Built Maslow's Pyramid?
sources.author_or_publisher: Todd Bridgman, Stephen Cummings, and John Ballard; Academy of Management Learning & Education
sources.supports: Historical finding that Maslow did not create the familiar pyramid and that later management teaching simplified a more complex and weakly supported theory.
sources.limitations: Focuses on visual and educational history rather than the whole late collection.

sources.title: Whatever Happened to Synanon? The Birth of the Anticriminal Therapeutic Community Methodology
sources.author_or_publisher: Office of Justice Programs / National Criminal Justice Reference Service
sources.supports: Historical account of Synanon's therapeutic-community origins and decline as it became an all-inclusive utopian organisation.
sources.limitations: Abstract record; the later decline occurred after Maslow's favourable observation.

sources.title: New Light on Maslow's Discovery of Daoism
sources.author_or_publisher: Edward Hoffman; Journal of Humanistic Psychology
sources.supports: Context for Toward a Humanistic Biology, its good-person and good-society research agenda, Daoist influence, and place among Maslow's final writings.
sources.limitations: Short, sympathetic historical reaction rather than empirical evaluation.

workflow.coverage_notes: Complete contents and searchable text were checked against library records, contemporary reviews, Maslow's self-critique, historical scholarship, modern motivation research, cross-cultural data, and the later history of a featured institution. Direct retrieval of one hosted scan timed out, so no claim of full-book verification is made.
